source_title: Tiger Shroff firing case: MCOCA court remands 11 accused in police custody till November 6
source_excerpt: Mumbai A special MCOCA court in Mumbai on Thursday (October 29, 2026) remanded all eleven accused in the actor Tiger Shroff firing case in police custody till November 6. The accused were produced before special judge Satyanarayan Navandar after being re-arrested under the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA). The police on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) invoked MCOCA provisions against the 11 people arrested so far in connection with the October 18 incident of firing on Mr. Shroff’s car in Mumbai’s Juhu area. Under the MCOCA, a court can grant bail only if it is satisfied that there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused is not guilty. Police get up to 180 days, instead of 90 days under ordinary criminal law, to file a chargesheet under the Act, and they can also seek longer custody of the accused. Confessions recorded before an officer of Deputy Commissioner of Police rank are admissible as evidence in court in MCOCA cases. Under ordinary criminal law, only confessions recorded before a magistrate are admissible.
